facts.text: Chatham-Kent's agri-food sector employed 7,935 people through 2,806 local agri-food business establishments in 2021.
facts.evidence: The local agri-food sector employed 7,935 people through 2,806 local agri-food business establishments in 2021.

facts.text: Chatham-Kent has more than 630,000 acres of farmland, more than 2,400 farms and over 20 million square feet of greenhouse space.
facts.evidence: Chatham-Kent is a leader in agricultural production, with more than 630,000 acres of farmland, more than 2,400 farms, and over 20-million square-feet of greenhouse space.

facts.text: Chatham-Kent ranks first in Canada for tomato, seed corn and pumpkin production.
facts.evidence: Chatham-Kent is #1 in tomato production, seed corn production, pumpkin production, and a top producer of carrots, cucumbers, and black tobacco in all of Canada.

facts.text: Chatham-Kent was created in 1998 by amalgamating 23 former municipalities, including Chatham, Wallaceburg, Tilbury, Blenheim, Ridgetown and Dresden.
facts.evidence: The City of Chatham (incorporated 1895) and Kent County (created 1792) are just two of the 23 former municipalities that comprise Chatham-Kent. overview: Chatham-Kent counted 103,988 residents in 2021, up 2.3% from 101,647 in 2016. The median household income was $72,000 in 2020, and spending is shaped by a large farm and food-processing economy.

Customers are spread across Chatham, Wallaceburg, Tilbury and many smaller towns, so most people search before they drive. A local business here competes less on novelty and more on being known, trusted and easy to reach across a wide rural area.
